API Reference

Abbreviations used on this page (TSDB, WAL, TTL, HWM, XPUB, ZMQ, SQLite, JSON, CLI, API, RSS, fd, PEP, CORS, OBS...) are defined in the Abbreviations & jargon section.

There are four ways to use sqtseries: the embedded Python API (in-process), the Client (remote), the CLI, and the wire protocol (ZMQ + HTTP). This page lists them all; if you are new, the Quick Start is a gentler entry point.

Time units at a glance. Embedded API: nanoseconds everywhere. ZMQ wire: ingest timestamps seconds; query start/end nanoseconds. HTTP gateway: start/end seconds. Query results are always seconds.

1. Embedded Python API (in-process)

sqtseries is embeddable: run the engine directly inside your own Python process, with no network involved. All timestamps here are nanoseconds.

from sqtseries.engine import (
    create_sqlite_engine,
    initialize_schema,
    run_migrations,
    StorageEngine,
)
from sqtseries.query import TimeSeriesDB

engine = create_sqlite_engine("~/.sqtseries/data/db.sqlite")
initialize_schema(engine)
run_migrations(engine)
ts = TimeSeriesDB(StorageEngine(engine))

# write (server-side timestamp by default; or pass timestamp_ns)
ts.insert("cpu.usage", 0.72, {"host": "web1"})
ts.insert("cpu.usage", 0.65, {"host": "web1"}, timestamp_ns=1720000000000000000)

# query -> [(timestamp_ns, value), ...]
rows = ts.query("cpu.usage", start=..., end=...,
                aggregation="avg", interval="15m", limit=100, order="asc")
# aggregation only -> one value over the window
one = ts.query("cpu.usage", aggregation="max")

# whole-window aggregations -> {func: value}
stats = ts.aggregate("cpu.usage", funcs=["avg", "min", "max", "p95"])

# convenience downsample (default interval 5m)
series = ts.downsample("cpu.usage", start=..., end=..., interval="5m", aggregation="avg")

# query by series_id (fastest path to isolate one host) and gap filling
sids = ts.store.series_ids_for_metric("cpu.usage")
rows = ts.query(series_ids=[sids[0]], start=..., end=...)
filled = ts.query("cpu.usage", start=..., end=..., fill_gaps_ns=60 * 10 ** 9)

# stream large results in bounded memory
for ts_ns, value in ts.query_stream("cpu.usage", start=..., end=...):
    process(ts_ns, value)

# maintenance / admin
from sqtseries.engine import run_optimize, backup_database, quick_check, wal_checkpoint
run_optimize(engine)
path = backup_database(engine, "~/.sqtseries/backups")
status = quick_check(engine)
wal_checkpoint(engine, "TRUNCATE")

2. Python Client (remote)

Connect to a running service. Default host 127.0.0.1 and ports {"write": 12501, "query": 12502, "subscribe": 12503, "admin": 12504}; override with Client(host=..., ports={...}) (the dict is merged over the defaults).

from sqtseries import Client

c = Client()

c.write("cpu.usage", 0.72, {"host": "web1"})      # timestamp: epoch SECONDS
c.write_many([{"metric": "cpu.usage", "value": 1.0},
              {"metric": "mem.usage", "value": 512.0, "tags": {"host": "web1"}}])

# query start/end: epoch NANOSECONDS; rows are [{timestamp_seconds, value}]
import time
now_ns = time.time_ns()
rows = c.query("cpu.usage", start=now_ns - 3600 * 10**9, end=now_ns,
               aggregation="avg", interval="15m", limit=100, order="desc")

stats = c.aggregate("cpu.usage", funcs=["avg", "max", "p95"])   # {func: value}

for payload in c.subscribe("cpu."):     # yields dicts, or None when idle
    if payload is not None:
        print(payload)

c.admin("stats")                         # see §5 Admin
c.close()                                # idempotent; `with Client() as c:` works too

ClientError is raised when a query, aggregate, or admin command receives an error reply (the server's message is attached), or when no reply arrives within the client's 30-second receive timeout (zmq.RCVTIMEO).

3. CLI Reference

Global options come before the subcommand: --config PATH (TOML/YAML/JSON), --db PATH (database file override — wins over config and env), --version (show version and exit).

Serve the service with your own config (own ports, own database); the same command works via python3 -m, which the scripts and systemd unit use:

sqtseries --config config.toml run
python3 -m sqtseries --config config.toml run
sqtseries --config config.toml --db /var/lib/tsdb.sqlite run
sqtseries --config config.toml install     # systemd runs that same config

run and stop refuse to act when the resolved database conflicts with a live instance's (see Configuration, "Choosing a database").

Service

sqtseries run              # start service (foreground)
sqtseries stop             # SIGTERM to the running service (via runtime file)
sqtseries status           # pid, version, db, ports
sqtseries ports            # active ports (or configured when not running)
sqtseries health           # database integrity probe; exit 0 = healthy

Database maintenance

sqtseries stats            # metric + series counts
sqtseries vacuum           # shrink the file (run while the service is stopped)
sqtseries optimize         # refresh query-planner statistics
sqtseries backup           # consistent snapshot via VACUUM INTO
                           #   (see backup.html: restore + vacuum guide)

Systemd

sqtseries install          # write + enable --now (user unit)
sqtseries install --system # system unit (root)
sqtseries uninstall        # disable + remove the unit

4. Wire protocol (ZMQ)

Ingest — PUSH 12501

{"metric": "cpu.usage", "tags": {"host": "web1"}, "value": 0.72, "timestamp": 1720000000.1}

Fire-and-forget, one frame per measurement, no reply and no ZMQ-level batching on the wire (the server drains frames in bursts and commits one transaction per burst). timestamp is optional epoch seconds (float allowed); skewed timestamps are rejected (default ±300s — dropped and counted as invalid on this path). The ingest port is auto-detected by default (ports.auto_detect): the first free port in 12500–12700, so it is usually 12500, not 12501 (the configured 12501 is used only with auto_detect = false).

Query — REQ 12502

→ {"type": "query", "metric": "cpu.usage",
   "start": 1720000000000000000, "end": 1720003600000000000,
   "aggregation": "avg", "interval": "15m", "limit": 100, "order": "asc"}
← {"status": "ok", "data": [{"timestamp": 1720000000.0, "value": 0.72}]}

Or whole-window multi-func (comma-separated aggregations — note the plural key; the reply's data becomes a dict): {"type": "query", "metric": "cpu.usage", "aggregations": "avg,min,max,p95"} → {"status": "ok", "data": {"avg": 0.71, ...}}. start/end are epoch nanoseconds, inclusive; omitting them queries all time.

5. Admin — REQ 12504

Send {"cmd": "..."} to the admin socket (ZMQ REP, port 12504). Errors use the standard error shape {"status":"error","error":{"code":...,"message":...}}.

Heavy commands pause the service briefly. Admin handlers run synchronously in the single worker loop, so a large backup or vacuum blocks ingestion and queries for its duration. For anything beyond a quick tidy, use the offline CLI (sqtseries backup / sqtseries vacuum) instead — see Backup & Restore.
CommandRequestReply
ping {"cmd":"ping"} {"status":"ok","pong":true}
health {"cmd":"health"} {"status":"ok","version":"0.1.0","uptime":123,"database":true} (status is "degraded" and database false when the DB integrity probe fails; uptime is integer seconds)
stats {"cmd":"stats"} {"status":"ok","uptime_s":...,"ingested":...,"invalid":...,"ingest_errors":...,"queries":...,"admin_requests":...,"published":...,"subscribers":...,"series":...,"metrics":...,"wal_bytes":...,"checkpoint_busy_runs":...,"checkpoints":...,"analyze_runs":...,"retention_runs":...,"partitions_dropped":...,"backup_runs":...,"backups_created":...,"last_backup":...,"query_cache_size":...,"query_cache_hits":...,"query_cache_misses":...} (uptime_s in seconds; counters reset on restart; backup_runs/backups_created appear when the scheduled backup task is enabled; last_backup appears only after the first snapshot succeeds; query_cache_size/hits/misses track the LRU query result cache — identical queries within the TTL are served from cache, avoiding redundant SQLite scans)
connections {"cmd":"connections"} {"status":"ok","data":[{id,kind,peer,topic,connected_at}]} — active WebSocket connections, oldest first
conncheck {"cmd":"conncheck","ids":["id1","id2"]} {"status":"ok","present":["id1"]} — which ids are still connected
subscribers {"cmd":"subscribers"} {"status":"ok","zmq_subscribers":N,"subscriptions":[{"topic":"cpu.","subscribers":2}]}
optimize {"cmd":"optimize"} {"status":"ok","optimized":true} (refresh query-planner statistics)
backup {"cmd":"backup"} {"status":"ok","path":"/…/sqtseries-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.db"} (consistent VACUUM INTO snapshot in backup.path; failure → BACKUP_FAILED)
vacuum {"cmd":"vacuum"} {"status":"ok","vacuumed":true}, or VACUUM_BUSY while running — stop the service and use sqtseries vacuum

An unknown or malformed command is answered with INVALID_REQUEST: {"status":"error","error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"unknown admin command: foo"}}.

import zmq, orjson
ctx = zmq.Context()
s = ctx.socket(zmq.REQ)
s.setsockopt(zmq.RCVTIMEO, 30000)
s.connect("tcp://127.0.0.1:12504")
s.send(orjson.dumps({"cmd": "stats"}))
print(orjson.loads(s.recv()))

5b. Stats PUB socket — 12506

sqtseries emits connection and subscription events on a separate ZMQ PUB socket (port 12506). Any ZMQ SUB client can subscribe to receive them in real time, using prefix filters or subscribing to all events with b"":

Event typeFieldsWhen
conn connect: id, kind ("ws"), peer, topic, connected_at, connected: true, ttl (60)
disconnect: id, kind, peer, topic, connected: false, connected_at, left_at		 A WebSocket client connects or disconnects (leave carries arrival + leaving times)
sub join: kind ("zmq"), topic, subscribers, arrived_at, ttl (30)
leave: kind, topic, subscribers, left_at, first_seen (no ttl)		 A ZMQ SUB subscriber joins or leaves a topic (leave carries leaving time + when the topic first became active)
report uptime_s, ws_connections, zmq_subscribers, active_topics Every 10 seconds
import zmq, json

ctx = zmq.Context()
sub = ctx.socket(zmq.SUB)
sub.connect("tcp://127.0.0.1:12506")
sub.setsockopt(zmq.SUBSCRIBE, b"conn")  # or b"" for all events

while True:
    event_type, payload = sub.recv_multipart()
    data = json.loads(payload)
    print(f"{event_type.decode()}: {data}")

6. HTTP API

Method + PathParams / BodyReturns
POST /api/v1/write JSON object or array of measurements (timestamp in seconds). A batch is validated whole — one bad item rejects the whole request. The same clock-skew guard as the ZMQ path applies: timestamps more than ingestion.reject_client_timestamp_skew_s (default 300s) from the server clock are rejected with 400. {"status":"ok","written":N}; 400 on invalid rows
GET /api/v1/read metric (req), start, end (seconds), aggregation, interval, limit (1–100000), order (asc|desc) {"status":"ok","data":[{timestamp,value}]}
GET /api/v1/aggregate metric (req), start, end (seconds), funcs (comma list, default avg) {"status":"ok","aggregations":{func:value}}
GET /api/v1/stats — {"status":"ok","metrics":N,"series":M}
GET /api/v1/connections — live active WebSocket connections, oldest first: {"status":"ok","data":[{id,kind,peer,topic,connected_at}]}
GET /api/v1/subscribers — live ZMQ subscriptions: {"status":"ok","zmq_subscribers":N,"subscriptions":[{topic,subscribers,first_seen}]}
GET /api/v1/health — {"status":"ok","version":"0.1.0"} when the SQLite database passes quick_check; {"status":"degraded","version":"0.1.0"} otherwise. This is a live DB probe, not just a port check.
WS /ws/subscribe?metric=PREFIX single topic prefix; * or omitted for all. Not a comma-separated list. Path is /ws/subscribe, not under /api/v1. streams {metric,tags,value} (no timestamp); {"type":"ping"} keepalives every ~30s of idle; close code 1008 "streaming disabled" if the pubsub bus is off
WS /ws/connections live connection/subscription feed — no query params {"type":"snapshot",...} on connect, then one frame per change: {"type":"conn", ...,"connected":true/false} (ws clients) and {"type":"sub",...} (zmq subscribers), pushed instantly. Conn frames carry connected_at and (on leave) left_at; sub frames carry arrived_at/left_at and first_seen
GET /dashboard live admin page (same origin as the API) self-contained HTML dashboard: service health, ingest/query rates, connections, topics, storage, event feed. See Dashboard.
WS /ws/dashboard dashboard push channel — no query params {"type":"snapshot",...} (counters, lists, storage) on connect, then live conn/sub events plus a {"type":"tick",...} with fresh counters every second. Listener unhooked and tick cancelled on disconnect.

Every response carries an X-Request-ID header (echoed from the request, or a fresh one). The gateway is rate-limited per client peer (default 600 requests/minute, http.rate_limit_per_minute) and CORS-enabled (http.cors_origins, default *). The rate limiter deliberately ignores the X-Forwarded-For header (it is client-supplied and spoofable), so all clients behind a reverse proxy share the proxy's limit — size the limit accordingly.

WebSocket resilience: the server limits one inbound frame to 16 MiB (ws_max_size; a larger frame closes the connection with code 1009), pings the peer every 20s at the protocol level (20s timeout) to drop dead connections, and evicts a subscriber that cannot accept a frame within 30s (close 1011 "slow consumer"). New connections beyond http.max_websocket_connections (default 1000) are accepted and immediately closed with code 1013 "try again later", so a connection flood cannot exhaust memory. Per-connection memory is bounded (ZMQ receive HWM of 1000 frames); a slow subscriber is dropped at the HWM rather than stalling other subscribers.

7. Error codes

Error replies share the shape {"status":"error","error":{"code":...,"message":...}}. The table below lists every error the wire can produce.

Code / StatusWhereWhenMessage (example)
INVALID_REQUESTZMQ queryJSON parse failureinvalid JSON: ...
INTERNAL_ERRORZMQ queryRequest is not an object (the broker calls the handler directly; non-objects crash the parser)'str' object has no attribute 'get'
INVALID_QUERYZMQ queryMissing metric and series_idseither metric or series_ids required
INVALID_QUERYZMQ querystart/end not numeric'<' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'str'
INVALID_REQUESTZMQ adminMessage is not an objectadmin message must be an object
INVALID_REQUESTZMQ adminMissing / empty / non-string cmdadmin cmd must be a non-empty string
INVALID_REQUESTZMQ adminUnknown commandunknown admin command: foo
INVALID_QUERYZMQ queryEngine rejects the query (unknown aggregation, bad interval, overflow)unsupported aggregation: bogus, unsupported interval: 5x, interval must be >= 1: 0m
QUERY_TIMEOUTZMQ queryQuery exceeded query.timeout_s (default 30s; server-side budget)query exceeded 30.0s
INTERNAL_ERRORZMQ queryUnexpected server error (also logged)exception text
NOT_READYZMQ queryQuery engine still startingquery engine unavailable
NOT_READYZMQ adminService still startingservice unavailable
BACKUP_FAILEDZMQ adminbackup could not create the snapshotexception text
VACUUM_BUSYZMQ adminvacuum failed while the service is runningvacuum failed while running; stop the service and use `sqtseries vacuum`: ...
400HTTP writeBody is not an object or arraybody must be an object or array
400HTTP writeAn array item is not an objecteach write must be an object
400HTTP writeMissing / empty / non-string metricmetric must be a non-empty string
400HTTP writeValue is not a number (booleans rejected)value must be a number
400HTTP writeNaN / ±Inf valuevalue must be finite
400HTTP writeTags are not a string→string objecttags must be string->string object
400HTTP writeTimestamp is not a numbertimestamp must be a number
400HTTP writeNaN / ±Inf timestamptimestamp must be finite
400HTTP writeTimestamp beyond the signed 64-bit nanosecond storage range (or too large to convert to a float)timestamp out of range
400HTTP writeClock skew beyond the guardclient timestamp skew exceeds 300.0s
400HTTP read / aggregateEngine rejects the parameters: unknown aggregation, or an invalid interval used together with an aggregation (a bare invalid interval with no aggregation is silently ignored)unsupported aggregation: bogus etc.
422HTTPParameter validation: missing required metric, limit outside 1–100000, order not asc/desc, non-numeric start/endFastAPI validation detail
429 RATE_LIMITEDHTTPMore than http.rate_limit_per_minute (default 600) requests in a minute from one clienttoo many requests
504HTTP read / aggregateQuery exceeded the server-side budget (query.timeout_s, default 30s). Queries run off the event loop in a thread, so this only times out that request — health, streaming, and other requests stay responsivequery exceeded 30.0s
close 1008WebSocketStreaming disabled (pubsub not running)streaming disabled

ZMQ ingest is different: bad messages are dropped, never answered (the PUSH path has no reply). Each drop reason below is counted in the admin stats reply (invalid / ingest_errors):

  • invalid JSON: ... — JSON parse failure
  • ingest message must be an object — top-level type wrong
  • metric must be a non-empty string — bad metric
  • value must be a number / value must be finite — bad value
  • tags must be an object / tags must be string->string — bad tags
  • timestamp must be a number / timestamp must be finite — bad timestamp
  • client timestamp skew Ns exceeds Ns — clock-skew guard
  • Frame larger than ingestion.max_message_size (50 MiB) — dropped at the socket level, peer disconnected
  • Send HWM full (default 10000) — the producer blocks on a blocking send() (backpressure, not an error)

The Python Client raises sqtseries.client.ClientError when a query, aggregate, or admin command returns an error reply, and when no reply arrives within its 30-second receive timeout. HTTP 400/422 messages are returned in the response body, not as this error shape.

8. Background tasks

TaskInterval (default)What it does
Rollup5mPre-aggregates completed hours into rollup_hourly for the query fast path; hours are only rolled once they are at least the client-skew window past completion
Retention1hDrops monthly partitions older than retention.default_ttl (30d) and their rollup rows
Maintenance1hRuns ANALYZE to refresh query-planner statistics
Checkpoint60sKeeps the WAL file bounded; warns when readers block it
